newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian shares mixed as first index published.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian shares mixed as first index published.

text.p: Palestinian shares closed mixed on Sunday and trading was heavy enough for the nascent Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE) to publish its first index.
The "Jerusalem Index", which started from a base value of 100, closed at 100.06 on a volume of 240,138 shares.
"Ten companies were traded today, but we have 15 companies trading regularly," said Safwan Bataina, PSE general manager.
The exchange also moved to two trading sessions a week -- Sundays and Wednesdays -- to accommodate the increased trading.

Bataina said volume in this week's two sessions could hit an all-time high if Wednesday's session sees similar trading volume. The market peaked two weeks ago with 454,250 shares worth 809,845 dinars changing hands.
"We're showing continuous improvement in the volume of trading and the number of investors despite the adverse political circumstances," Bataina said.
Palestinian-Israeli peace talks have been frozen since March with intermittent clashes between Palestinians and Israelis in the West Bank and Gaza.
Bataina said were it not for the clashes, the volume of trade would be higher.
"There's very little investment demand out there, since the political environment turned sour," Bataina said. "In spite of all this, we're showing increases."

In trading this week, the Palestine Telecommunications Co., which accounted for almost 92 percent of the total turnover, closed up 0.70 percent to 1.43 dinars per share. The Arab Co. for Paint Products also rose 3.85 percent to 1.32 dinars per share.
Six other companies showed losses, and two were unchanged.
Trading is conducted in dollars or Jordanian dinars in absence of a Palestinian currency.
